workflow_runs.display_title: app-server: expose loaded thread status via read/list and notifications

head_commit.message:
app-server: add robust thread/watch state view for loaded threads

Motivation:
- Today there is no mechanism to know whether a loaded thread is waiting on
  permission approval/user input, currently running, or failed unless that
  specific thread is resumed from the current connection.
- This change adds a watchable high-level thread-state view so each connection
  does not need to resume all loaded threads just to observe runtime status.

Add a new `thread/watch` v2 RPC that returns an atomic snapshot
(`snapshotVersion` + `data`) and then streams versioned
`thread/watch/updated` deltas.

Key behavior and design updates:
- Introduce typed loaded-thread status modeling:
  - `idle`
  - `active` with `running`, `waitingPermission`, `waitingUserInput`
  - `terminal` with `completed`, `failed`, `interrupted`, `shutdown`
- Add `ThreadWatchManager` to maintain loaded-thread runtime facts and publish
  monotonic updates.
- Consolidate descendant runtime blockers into root-thread active flags so
  clients get a single root-oriented state view that is easier to consume.
- Keep root terminal outcome sourced from the root thread itself (descendant
  failures do not overwrite root terminal outcome).
- Emit `resyncRequired` when broadcast lag is detected; this update is terminal
  for the current subscription and clients recover by re-issuing `thread/watch`.
- Strip turn history from watch snapshots/deltas to keep payloads lightweight and
  focused on state.

Wire thread/watch state updates through server lifecycle and event handling:
- thread upsert/remove paths (start/resume/fork/review start/archive/collab close,
  plus loaded-thread listener attach paths)
- turn lifecycle (started/completed/interrupted/shutdown)
- permission and user-input waits via guard-backed counters

Also update protocol registrations/schemas/TypeScript exports, document the API
and root-state semantics in `app-server/README.md`, and add focused unit +
integration coverage for:
- snapshot/version ordering and atomic subscribe semantics
- active/terminal transitions and guard release behavior
- lag -> `resyncRequired` recovery behavior
- archive/remove and unarchive/resume re-upsert flows
- notification opt-out behavior

head_commit.message:
fix(linux-sandbox): stabilize proxy-routed seccomp on CI

Use explicit AF_UNIX-equality rules for proxy-routed seccomp instead of composing multiple comparisons on the same syscall argument. This keeps managed proxy mode aligned with the AF_UNIX lockdown requirement while avoiding the runtime failure path seen in Linux CI. Also removes an unnecessary unsafe block in loopback setup.

Co-Authored-By: Codex <199175422+chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>
